provenance: Regions from the independent initial assessment of the exact candidate.

issues.label: Upward blade face remains ambiguous at the first active drawing
issues.reason: At 1:1 the mostly horizontal curved saber reads clearly as the same narrow saber with a somewhat stronger upper highlight. At close-up, the white strip is easier to distinguish from a darker lower facet, but the perceived change in plane is too small to establish the target on the native-size still. Hilt-to-blade contact and projected width are preserved.
issues.observable_condition: An independent matched native-size comparison can recognize the upward-facing surface at the first active pose without relying on magnification, while the weapon remains slender and visually continuous.

issues.label: Second active drawing does not resolve blade facing
issues.reason: The close-up shows a clean bright strip above a stronger dark strip, but at 1:1 this mostly reads as a contrast adjustment on the same rearward curved silhouette. The blade still appears contiguous with its guard, and there is no new width or registration defect in the blade.
issues.observable_condition: The same upward-facing interpretation remains apparent when the rearward blade lowers into drawing 6. A watched matched clip is needed to assess whether it reads through the transition.

issues.label: Existing horizontal mount and rider seams are still visible
issues.reason: Frame 6 has stepped horizontal joins through the horse's tail and saddle cloth and through the rider's upper leg and reins. These are visible in the matched whole-pose still and unmistakable in the 3× crop. The regions are pixel-identical between R04 and Trial 1, and there is no introduced hoof or body offset.
issues.observable_condition: If addressed within an authorized iteration, the tail, cloth, thigh and reins read continuously at the join and keep the same registered pose.

improvements.label: Clearer upper and lower steel tones in close-up
improvements.reason: At close-up the candidate shifts emphasis to the upper highlight and darkens the lower band in drawings 5 and 6, making the subtle top-versus-underside distinction sharper.
